title: Staged compatibility gates for isolated deployments: release sprints, SLAs, and acceptance
creator: Monica Alvarez
description:
Problem statement: Enterprise customers deploying Redwood Private/VPC require a predictable, auditable release cadence with explicit compatibility gates (component compatibility, KMS/HSM certs, kernel/quantization profiles, and autoscaler policies). Current ambiguity in acceptance criteria is causing delayed upgrades and increased SE time for each customer.

Goal: Define and land a staged set of compatibility gates, corresponding engineering sprints, and explicit SLA commitments so that Private customers can adopt upgrades with a clear risk profile. Deliverables for the quarter include: a compatibility matrix v1, CI/QA automation for isolation smoke tests, a gated canary runbook, SLA language for Dedicated/Private contracts, and an internal preflight checklist used by Solutions Engineering and Onboarding.

Success metrics (OKR mapping):
- OKR: Reduce upgrade-assisted customer hours by 60% (Metric: mean SE-hours per upgrade)
- OKR: Increase upgrade adoption rate within 90 days to 70% for eligible customers (Metric: % customers migrated)
- OKR: Prevent regressions in P99 tail latency during canary (Metric: P99 delta <= 10%)

Scope: Compatibility gates cover runtime versions, quantization/weight formats, autoscaler policy compatibility, RBAC/audit log schema, KMS key reference formats, and console API contract stability. Excludes model version policy (handled in Model Onboarding).
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility matrix v1 published and approved by Eng/SE/Security
Automated isolation smoke tests run in customer-like VPCs with pass/fail report
Canary runbook and escalation path documented and validated in rehearsal
SLA wording drafted and approved by Legal for private upgrade windows
Preflight checklist available in Console UI for Solutions Engineers
Zero critical regressions found in two consecutive canary cohorts
